title: Variables & Real I/O Declaration
concept:
Every tag you use must be declared with a **type** in a `VAR ... END_VAR` block:

- **BOOL**: one bit, TRUE/FALSE (a coil, a contact, a lamp).
- **INT / DINT**: whole numbers (counts, steps). AB defaults to 32-bit DINT. A Siemens INT is 16-bit.
- **REAL**: decimals (an analog level, a temperature).

But real controls care about more than the type. They care **how each field device is wired**, because that decides how you read it in code.

## N.O. vs N.C., the contact type

A pushbutton or switch is either **Normally Open (N.O.)** or **Normally Closed (N.C.)**:

- **N.O.**: open at rest, closes when actuated. Its input bit is FALSE at rest, TRUE when actuated. Typical: start buttons, photo-eyes.
- **N.C.**: closed at rest, opens when actuated (or when the wire breaks). Its input bit is TRUE at rest, FALSE when actuated. Typical fail-safe devices: stop, E-stop, overloads, guards.

## XIC vs XIO, how you read it

Two instructions describe how you examine a bit (Allen-Bradley names, but the idea is universal):

- **XIC** = Examine If Closed → in Structured Text you use the tag as-is (`Tag`). TRUE when the bit is 1.
- **XIO** = Examine If Open → in Structured Text you use `NOT Tag`. TRUE when the bit is 0.

Contact type is about the **device**; XIC/XIO is about how you **read** it. The key move: safety devices are wired **N.C. and fail-safe**, energized (bit = 1) when healthy, so you read them with **XIC** and AND them into the rung as-is. A broken wire de-energizes the input and safely stops the machine. Reach for **XIO** (`NOT`) only when you truly need the inverted state: an edge-detect memory bit, or a signal that is TRUE when bad.

From here on, every tag is labeled **(N.O.)** or **(N.C.)** with its XIC/XIO reading, so the distinction becomes second nature.
ab_note:
In Studio 5000 the default integer is DINT (32-bit) -- the Logix processor is
32-bit native. Discrete field inputs come in as BOOL tags aliased to input
module points; the contact type (N.O./N.C.) is a wiring fact you record in the
tag description.
siemens_note:
In TIA Portal / SCL, INT is a true 16-bit type (-32768..+32767) and DINT is
32-bit. Field I/O is declared in the block interface (VAR / VAR_INPUT /
VAR_OUTPUT) and mapped to PLC tags in the tag table.
task:
Declare a VAR ... END_VAR block with these six tags for a motor station,
using the correct types:

    Start_PB   : BOOL        (N.O. start pushbutton)
    Stop_PB    : BOOL        (N.C. stop pushbutton)
    Motor_OL   : BOOL        (N.C. overload aux contact)
    Motor_Run  : BOOL        (output to contactor)
    Part_Count : DINT := 0   (initialize to 0 with := )
    Tank_Level : REAL

Add a short comment on at least one line noting its contact type.
starter:
(* Lesson 01 -- Variables & Real I/O Declaration *)
(* Declare each field device with its TYPE and note its CONTACT TYPE.        *)
(* Wiring key:  N.O. contact -> read AS-IS (XIC)   |   N.C. contact -> AS-IS, fail-safe (XIC)   |   NOT x = XIO *)
VAR
    (* TODO: declare each tag with the right type (BOOL / DINT / REAL):      *)
    (*   Start_PB   (N.O. start pushbutton)                                  *)
    (*   Stop_PB    (N.C. stop pushbutton)                                   *)
    (*   Motor_OL   (N.C. overload aux)                                      *)
    (*   Motor_Run  (contactor output)                                       *)
    (*   Part_Count (production counter, DINT, start at 0)                   *)
    (*   Tank_Level (analog level 0.0-100.0 %, REAL)                         *)
END_VAR

checks.message: Uses a VAR ... END_VAR declaration block
checks.hint: Wrap declarations between VAR and END_VAR.

checks.message: Declares Start_PB as BOOL (N.O. start PB)
Declares Stop_PB as BOOL (N.C. stop PB)
Declares Motor_OL as BOOL (N.C. overload aux)
Declares Part_Count as DINT initialized to 0
Includes a comment documenting a device
checks.hint: Add a comment, e.g. Stop_PB : BOOL; (* N.C. stop pushbutton *)

solution:
(* Lesson 01 -- Variables & Real I/O Declaration *)
(* Wiring key:  N.O. contact -> read AS-IS (XIC)   |   N.C. contact -> AS-IS, fail-safe (XIC)   |   NOT x = XIO *)
VAR
    Start_PB   : BOOL;      (* N.O. start pushbutton  -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when pressed      *)
    Stop_PB    : BOOL;      (* N.C. stop pushbutton   -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when NOT pressed  *)
    Motor_OL   : BOOL;      (* N.C. overload aux      -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when healthy      *)
    Motor_Run  : BOOL;      (* output to the motor contactor                                *)
    Part_Count : DINT := 0; (* production counter                                           *)
    Tank_Level : REAL;      (* analog level 0.0-100.0 %                                      *)
END_VAR
